  Exam Date & Time: 17-Nov-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  FIFTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  DATA ARCHITECTURE [DS_3151]  
  Marks: 50                                                                              Duration: 180 mins.  
  PART-A  
  Answer all the questions.  
  1)           A national energy company, "PowerGrid," collects two primary data types: (1) Billions  
  of smart meter readings and (2) Thousands of customer complaints left as free-form  
  notes in the CRM.  
  A)  
  Critically evaluate the difference in processing strategy between these two data streams  
  based on the "Great Divide".                                                                (5)  
  
  Explain why processing the meter readings is considered Hadoop-centric and relies on  
  parsing being "almost trivial," whereas the customer notes must emphasize Textual  
  Disambiguation.  
  
  B)      Analyze the role of Taxonomies in the analysis of the customer complaint notes. Explain  
  how a taxonomy allows PowerGrid to unify queries on a broad concept (e.g., "service  
  outage") even if only specific instances (e.g., "power cut," "cable down") appear in the (3)  
  original text.  
  
  C)      Apply the concept of Custom Variables or Named Value Processing to describe how  
  PowerGrid could automatically identify and tag a standard customer ID format  
  consistently embedded within the customer service notes based purely on format              (2)  
  recognition.  
  
  2)           A government agency is modernizing its systems. They are debating whether to use the  
  artifact-centric Zachman Framework or the process-centric TOGAF Architecture  
  Development Method (ADM)  
  A)      for guiding the modernization initiative.  
  (5)  
  Critically evaluate the difference in focus between the process-oriented TOGAF ADM  
  (as an iterative process, Phase A-H) and the artifact classification grid of the Zachman  
  Framework. Which framework is generally better suited for achieving rapid business  
  value?  
  
  B)      Analyze the architectural guiding principles: Evolution of the Object (extensibility) and  
  designing for Current and Future Use (repurposing). Explain why incorporating these       (3)  
  principles is vital for building systems that remain agile as business needs mature.  
  
  C)      Explain the purpose of Phase A: Architecture Vision in this context. Describe how it        (2)

  helps the team establish the project scope, identify key stakeholders, and gain  
  management approval before moving to the detailed design phases.  
  
  3)        NextGen's logical model includes complex entities like Employee that relate to  
  themselves, and requires detailed historical tracking for critical changes.  
  
  A)   Critically evaluate the necessity of Complex History (Historical Logging) over Simple (5)  
  or Bounded Simple History. Justify why Complex History is mandatory when the  
  integrity of the audit trail requires the capability to handle retroactive or out-of-sequence  
  changes.  
  
  B)   Analyze the problem of Recursive Relationships and how this structure can lead to  
  Duplicate Propagated Keys. Explain the resolution techniques needed: renaming the key (3)  
  or selectively removing the identifying nature of the relationship.  
  
  C)   Apply the concept of history by defining the implementation of Bounded Simple  
  History. Specifically, identify the two time-dependent keys required for tracking a non-    (2)  
  critical attribute change.  
  
  4)        FinTech manages its designs in a Model Repository. The logical model must be  
  transformed into a Physical Data Model (PDM) for an OLTP system, which must remain  
  separate from the Data Warehouse (DW).  
  A)                                                                                               (5)  
  Evaluate the necessity of a strict Model Repository Policy that governs Subsetting and  
  Reconciliation . Explain why reconciliation is crucial for reintegrating the application  
  PDM back into the Enterprise Logical Model.  
  
  B)   Analyze why OLTP Data Stores are fundamentally unsuitable for being used directly as  
  a Data Warehouse. Focus your analysis on the conflict between optimizing for  
  transactional performance versus high-volume DSS retrieval, and the requirement for  (3)  
  noncontention.  
  
  C)   Define the physical design concept of Horizontal Segmentation. Explain when this  
  technique is typically applied, using data volume, access patterns, or archiving needs as (2)  
  justification  
  
  5)        The physical design team at FinTech Solutions is conducting a final design review for its  
  Customer Account Management System. They are using Interaction Analysis tools  
  including the CRUD Matrix and the Entity Life Cycle Analysis (ELCA), to validate  
  A)   whether all business processes and data entities are correctly aligned.  
  Evaluate how these two tools complement each other in verifying the completeness and (5)  
  correctness of the system's design. Specifically, explain how the ELCA ensures that  
  every entity (e.g., Customer Account) transitions through all valid states, while the  
  CRUD Matrix validates that every process properly performs the required data  
  operations on the corresponding entities.

  B)            The database designer uses a Composite Load Map to visualize how multiple system  
  processes access shared data tables.  
  
  Analyze how this map helps identify Hot Spots (tables or columns accessed too           (3)  
  frequently) and define what Referential Groups and Unit of Work Constraints reveal  
  about the system's data access behavior.  
  
  C)            In a reporting database, too many small tables are slowing down queries.  
  
  Explain how Entity Consolidation can simplify the schema and improve query  
  performance.                                                                           (2)  
  Also describe one drawback of Overnormalisation that might lead to excessive joins and  
  loss of practical "data intelligence."
